links.outcome: F1 of fine-tuned small model versus commercial and open-source LLMs on same report sets
links.effect: On 500 real-world reports, fine-tuned model F1 70.32% ± 1.54% vs best LLM Gemini 2.5 Flash 58.22% ± 1.50% (p<0.001); on 350 cleaned reports GPT-5 (89.51 ± 1.52%) outperformed fine-tuned models.
links.quote: On a subset of 500 real-world samples, our models outperformed the best-performing LLM, Gemini 2.5 Flash, with an F1-score of 70.32% ± 1.54% compared to 58.22% ± 1.50% (p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning a small domain-specific LLM for billing code classification versus zero/few-shot prompting of large proprietary LLMs

screen.reason: The study benchmarks fine-tuned and commercial LLMs for automated billing code classification on retrospective radiology report datasets without evaluating a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
